why: no model has been rendered and compared with the unit
claim: The filter a stereo flanger puts in front of itself and the filter a stereo chorus puts in front of itself are one section. Swept at every setting the chorus's was published at -- 15 of them across the two filter shapes the byte beside it offers -- the two types return the same skirt over a hundred and thirteen twelfth-octave bands to a median of 0.08 dB at worst, where those runs repeat themselves to 0.08 dB and where one step of the byte being swept moves the profile by at least 0.15 dB. The agreement is at the floor and the thing it is being told from is two to ten times the floor, so this is the reading saying the same section twice and not the reading running out. The page prints the two types' parameter lists identically -- same order, same addresses, same ranges -- with one entry in the flanger's that the chorus has not got, a feedback level in the slot the chorus leaves empty. That list is what made the question worth asking and it is not what answers it; what this file claims is the front end, and what the loop is around is queued. The byte the flanger has and the chorus has not is a loop, and it is around the delay the byte beside it sets. A loop around a delay has to do three things and none of them is what a filter does, so each was asked separately and the modulator was parked at no rate and no depth throughout so that the delay stood still while they were. It puts teeth in the spectrum: 23.4 decibels of them at the ends of the byte, against 0.79 dB at the centre the page prints as nought -- so the printed nought is no loop rather than a small one. It deepens them without moving them: across the three settings either side where the teeth clear the run's own repeats, the delay read off the comb does not move at all while the depth goes from a third of its range to all of it. And it spaces them by the delay the byte beside it sets, which is the one that says the loop is around that delay and not around some second structure: at pre-delay 6 the comb reads 0.618 ms and at 13 it reads 1.318, a ratio of 2.133 where the byte's own is 2.167. That is the same delay per step of the byte in both places, 0.1022 ms, read two ways that did not have to agree. The loop's sign is the cheapest confirmation of all and it is there: below the printed nought the teeth sit halfway between where they sit above it, which is what an inverting loop does and what nothing else does. Scored as an inverting comb the negative settings beat the same profile scored as an in-phase one by 1.59 times at worst, and the delay each sign returns is the other's to within the width of the reading. The two modulators are not one, and the depth byte is what says so. The run this file queued was made three times, at the pre-delay a comb read at six tenths of a millisecond, near each type's own printed default, and at three times that. Read properly the three agree with each other to 2.98 per cent at every setting, which is the point: the pre-delay does not enter a pitch excursion at all, and three runs that differ in nothing that could move it returning one curve is what says the curve is the byte's. The setting each was asked twice at repeats to 2.74 per cent. Both curves rise with their own byte at every step. And they are not the same curve: the flanger swings 12.9, 27.5, 61.1, 100.7, 147.2 cents where the chorus swings 9.8, 19.3, 39.9, 66.4, 98.1, a ratio running from 1.316 to 1.501. One stage reached twice returns one excursion; these differ at every setting by two orders of magnitude more than either repeats to, and they differ by a ratio that is not constant, so it is not a gain in front of one modulator either. The front end is shared and the modulator is not.
adds: Each record says what one type's pre-filter byte does to a band profile. What is read out of the pair is that the two profiles are the same profile -- a comparison between records, made against a third figure neither record states, which is what one step of the swept byte is worth under the same reading.
refutedBy: The two pre-filters departing at a setting neither run asked -- the grid is eleven of a hundred and twenty-eight through the low pass and four through the high pass, so a table that agreed at those and not between them would look exactly like this. Or either type's filter turning out to move with something the other's does not: both runs parked the modulator and opened the loop, and a pre-filter that depended on either would have been read at one point of a surface rather than as a curve.
whatItWouldChange: Two of the sixty-four types stop being two front ends. One pre-filter section, one byte choosing between off, a low pass and a high pass, and one cutoff table, serve both -- and the cutoff table is the one the frequency class already closed.

It puts the question where it belongs. If the front ends are one section then what separates a chorus from a flanger on this unit is whatever the feedback byte reaches, and that is one run rather than a comparison of two whole types.

eraPriors.claim: A chorus and a flanger on a fixed-point part of this period are the same arithmetic: a short modulated delay summed with the dry signal, with the flanger differing by a path from the delay's output back to its input. Writing them as two stages costs two copies of the interpolator and the modulator for one extra multiply-accumulate of difference.
eraPriors.why: It says why one front end being shared is worth reading as the two types being one stage rather than as two stages that happen to filter alike. It carries none of the claim: what is claimed is the section the measurement reached.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The two front ends had differed. They did not, at fifteen settings across two filter shapes, by more than the runs repeat themselves.

alternatives.reading: Two separate filter sections written from one specification, rather than one section reached from two types.

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: Not applicable. The two readings predict the same output at every setting of every byte, so no sensitivity would help.
separatedBy.why_not_separable: Nothing leaving this unit's sockets distinguishes one routine called from two places from two routines computing the same numbers. The archive can say the responses are the same, which it does; what it cannot say is how many times the coefficients are stored. The era prior leans one way and a prior may not close a claim.

alternatives.reading: The flanger's extra parameter is a loop around the same delay line the chorus uses. Answered in half: it is a loop, and it is around the delay this type's own pre-delay byte sets. That the chorus reads from that same line is not measured and is recorded as what is still open rather than as what was shown.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Not ruled out -- carried, and then narrowed. The run made all three readings a loop owes: teeth twenty-three decibels deep where the printed nought gives under one, a delay that does not move while the byte deepens them, and a spacing that follows the pre-delay byte to 1.6 per cent. The sign flip is there as well. What it did not read is the chorus's delay, so the word the alternative turns on -- shared -- is the part left open.

separatedBy.observable: The decay of the flanger's response at several settings of `40 03 08`, with the modulator parked so the delay is fixed. A loop around a delay of d milliseconds puts its resonances at multiples of 1/d and makes them sharper as the byte goes up; the pre-delay byte then moves those resonances by exactly what it moves the delay by, which is what says the loop is around that delay rather than around something else.

predicts.a loop around the shared delay: A comb whose spacing is one over the pre-delay setting, moving with the pre-delay byte and sharpening with the feedback byte.
predicts.a second structure of its own: Resonances that do not move with the pre-delay byte, or do not space themselves by it.

separatedBy.divergence: The whole spacing of a comb, which at a pre-delay of a few milliseconds is hundreds of hertz.
separatedBy.sensitivity_here: A twelfth-octave band set separates 0.0847 octaves, which at the frequencies a comb of this spacing puts its teeth is far finer than one tooth.

run.stimulus: the same held note, modulator parked, pre-delay asked at two values so the comb has to move

alternatives.reading: The loop is around a delay of its own that happens to track the pre-delay byte, rather than around the delay that byte sets.

separatedBy.observable: Nothing this rig can reach. A delay of its own that follows the same byte returns the same comb at every setting of it, and a comb is the only thing the output can be asked.

predicts.one delay in a loop: teeth at multiples of one over the byte's delay

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: 1.6 per cent, which is how closely the spacing already follows the byte.
separatedBy.why_not_separable: It is the same shape of alternative the archive already carries for a table reached twice: two structures with the same arithmetic are one structure as far as an output goes. What the agreement does rule out is a loop around something the pre-delay byte does not move, which is what it was asked.
